output.entity_proposed: Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority (Authority)
output.proposal: HB No. 11202 seeks to enhance the protection and development of the Sierra Madre Range in Luzon by creating the Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority, a government corporation with jurisdiction over the Range and its surrounding areas in ten provinces, and defining its powers and functions.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure creating a new government corporation, the review should examine how the Authority's conservation, development and regulatory functions fit with those of existing agencies and bodies with mandates over the Sierra Madre, including the protected area established under RA No. 9125 for the Northern Sierra Madre in Isabela, and how the creation of a new corporate body relates to the government's intent to streamline agencies and reduce overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also assess the corporate and financing features of the Authority, including its power to borrow, its tax subsidy, the government guarantee and its supervision arrangements, in light of the role of the Governance Commission for GOCCs. No matching FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item was identified for the measure.
legislative_history: HB No. 11202 was filed on September 8, 2026, in the 20th Congress; later stages are not reflected in the available records.
HB No. 3538, filed on August 12, 2025, in the 20th Congress and pending in the Committee, carries the same title; its text has not been reviewed.
HB No. 1214, filed on July 5, 2022, in the 19th Congress and pending in the Committee, carries the same title; its text has not been reviewed.
HB No. 8305, filed on January 5, 2021, in the 18th Congress and pending in the Committee, also proposed a Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority; its text has not been reviewed.
HB No. 5634 (18th Congress) and HB No. 1972 (19th Congress), both pending in the Committee, proposed a Sierra Madre Development Authority for the Sierra Madre Region.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11202 seeks to create the Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority as a government corporation for the protection and development of the Sierra Madre Range. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 1 (Short Title) provides that the measure shall be cited as the Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority Act.
b. Section 3 (Creation of the Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority) provides for the creation of the Authority as a government corporation, to be organized within 90 days after the approval of the Act, with jurisdiction over the Sierra Madre Range and surrounding areas in the provinces of Cagayan, Isabela, Nueva Vizcaya, Quirino, Nueva Ecija, Aurora, Bulacan, Rizal, Laguna and Quezon.
c. Section 4 (Purposes and Functions of the Authority) and Section 5 (Regulatory Fees) set out the functions of the Authority and its regulatory fees.
d. Section 6 (Corporate Powers) provides that the Authority shall have the usual corporate powers, including the power to sue and be sued, enter into contracts, acquire and dispose of property, exercise eminent domain, borrow from local or foreign financial institutions, invest in securities subject to limits on high-risk instruments, and issue implementing rules subject to DEPDev approval and publication.
e. Section 7 (Capitalization and Financing), Section 8 (Operating Expenses), Section 9 (Tax Subsidy) and Section 10 (Guarantee by the Government) set out the financing of the Authority, its operating expenses, a tax subsidy and a government guarantee.
f. Section 11 (Subsidiaries) provides for subsidiaries of the Authority.
g. Section 12 (Board of Directors) to Section 16 (Power and Functions of the Board of Directors) provide for the Board of Directors, its meetings, quorum, per diems and allowances, and powers and functions.
h. Section 17 (Power and Functions of the General Manager) sets out the powers and functions of the General Manager.
i. Section 20 (Audit), Section 21 (Compensation), Section 22 (Authority of the Governance Commission on GOCCs), Section 23 (Legal Counsel) and Section 24 (Supervision) provide for audit, compensation, the role of the Governance Commission for GOCCs, legal counsel and supervision of the Authority.
j. Section 25 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides for the issuance of implementing rules.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11202 may be considered alongside HB No. 3538 of the same Congress and HB No. 1214 of the 19th Congress, which carry the same title, as well as HB No. 8305 of the 18th Congress and HB No. 5634 and HB No. 1972, which proposed similar Sierra Madre authorities; their texts should be compared to confirm the extent of similarity. No matching FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item was identified. The review should assess whether the Authority's jurisdiction under Section 3 (Creation of the Sierra Madre Conservation and Development Authority) overlaps with the management of the Northern Sierra Madre protected area under RA No. 9125, whether a new government corporation is warranted in light of streamlining under RA No. 12231, and the fiscal exposure arising from Section 6 (Corporate Powers), Section 9 (Tax Subsidy) and Section 10 (Guarantee by the Government).
